big_idea: Many addition and subtraction expressions equal the same number. 50 = 25+25 = 40+10 = 60-10 = 75-25.
learning_intention: We are learning to find many equivalent expressions for the same whole number up to 100.
student_learning_goal: I can find many equivalent expressions for the same whole number up to 100.
success_criteria: I can list 6+ different addition expressions that equal 50.
I can list 5+ different addition or subtraction expressions for any number up to 100.
I can use both addition and subtraction to make equivalent expressions.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dee and Mystery Mo — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Anchor chart 'Many Ways to Make 50' with 8+ expressions listed
Lesson 4 equivalent-expressions tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Detective Dee says 25 + 25 makes 50. Mystery Mo says 40 + 10 makes 50. Who's right?
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dee + Mystery Mo puppets. 'Friends — Detective Dee and Mystery Mo are arguing. Dee says 25 + 25 makes 50. Mo says 40 + 10 makes 50. Who's right?'

Take responses. 'Both!' 'Right — they're BOTH right. 25 + 25 = 50 AND 40 + 10 = 50. They're EQUIVALENT EXPRESSIONS — different ways to write the same number.'

Write on the chart:
50 = 25 + 25
50 = 40 + 10

'Today we're hunting for ALL the ways to make 50. Watch.'

Add more:
50 = 30 + 20
50 = 45 + 5
50 = 49 + 1
50 = 50 + 0
50 = 60 - 10 (subtraction works too)
50 = 75 - 25
50 = 100 - 50
50 = 25 + 15 + 10 (3 numbers also)
50 = 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 (5 numbers)

'Detective Dee says — there are MANY ways to make 50. Different expressions, SAME amount.'

Reinforce vocabulary. 'Equivalent means EQUAL. 25 + 25 and 40 + 10 are equivalent because they both equal 50.'

Now another target: 100. Build expressions: 100 = 50+50 = 75+25 = 90+10 = 60+40 = 100+0 = 150-50 = 200-100 = 25+25+25+25.

'Today we'll find many ways for many target numbers — 50, 75, even 100.'
student_actions: Predict who's right between Dee and Mo.
Help find more ways to make 50.

steps.instruction: Whole group: find 6+ expressions for 75. Examples: 50+25, 70+5, 80-5, 100-25, 25+25+25, 60+15.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Many ways to make 75. Who has one?' Take responses; record on chart.

steps.instruction: Send pairs to three stations (~7 min each). Station A: Make 50 — pair lists 8+ expressions for 50 on a worksheet. Station B: Make 100 — pair lists 6+ expressions for 100. Station C: Pick Your Target — pair picks a target between 60 and 100 and lists 5+ expressions.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Three stations, 7 minutes each.'

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge at Station C: include 3-term expressions (25+15+10 = 50). Discuss whether 3 addends count as equivalent expressions. (Yes — same total.)
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to pairs: 'You can use 2, 3, or more numbers. Same total, equivalent expression.'

steps.instruction: Discuss patterns. (a) Pairs that swap: 30+20 and 20+30 are commutative — same expression. (b) Adding/subtracting from neighbours: 25+25 ↔ 24+26 ↔ 23+27 — each move keeps the same total. (c) Subtraction: 60-10 = 50 = 25+25.
steps.teacher_prompt: Use the balance scale: 25+25 vs 40+10 — both balance with 50. Visual proof of equivalence.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the equivalent-expressions tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'How many ways did you find for 50?' Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use only sums under 50. Find 5+ ways to make 50 with addition only.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch to targets above 100 (e.g., make 200). Discuss whether the rule extends.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a structured chart with 8 blank rows under each target. Sentence frame: 'I made ___ with ___ + ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Use the balance scale physically — for each new way, build it on the scale and verify the balance.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: lists 6+ equivalent expressions for 50; lists 5+ for a number up to 100; uses both addition and subtraction.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the equivalent-expressions tracker per child.

discussion_prompts: How many ways did you find to make 50?
Can subtraction expressions equal 50? Give an example.
Can a 3-term expression equal 50? Give an example.
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes ONE equivalent expression for a target of their choice on a sticky note: '___ = ___ + ___' or '___ = ___ - ___'. Notes go on the chart.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Equivalent-expression generation count and variety (addition and subtraction, 2 and 3 terms).
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 4 captures C2.3 mastery for whole numbers up to 100. Children at L4 generate 6+ expressions including subtraction and 3-term combinations.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child lists 'equivalent' expressions that all use the same numbers (25+25, 25+25, 25+25) — repairing the variety-of-equivalence understanding
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-2 trap on C2.3 is the same-numbers-different-order trap: the child finds 25+25 = 50 and then writes 25+25 = 50 again, treating each rewrite as a new equivalence. They miss that the LIST should contain DIFFERENT addend pairs.

The distinction matters because C2.3 requires variety — the child must show they understand that the SAME total can be reached MANY DIFFERENT ways. The walkthrough covers the precise moment when a child writes the same expression repeatedly.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. The child lists for 50: '25+25, 25+25, 25+25, 25+25, 25+25'. Same expression five times.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch beside the child. 'You wrote 25+25 five times. That's just ONE way to make 50. Detective Dee wants you to find SIX DIFFERENT ways.' Pause. 'How else could you make 50?'

Wait. The child thinks. 'Maybe 30+20?' 'YES! 30+20 is a NEW way. Different addend pair. Write it.' Child writes.

'Now another. What else?' 'Maybe 50+0?' 'Right! 50 plus zero is also 50. Write it.' Continue.

Now the rule. 'Detective Dee says — to find DIFFERENT ways, change the addend pair. 25+25, 30+20, 40+10, 45+5, 50+0, 75-25 — all different addend pairs, all make 50.'

If the child STILL repeats: provide a sentence frame. 'For each way, write a NEW pair: ___ + ___ = 50. Pick numbers that aren't the same as before.' Build the variety reflex.

Long-term recovery: practice 'find 6 DIFFERENT ways' as a daily warm-up. Variety becomes the goal.
common_misconceptions: Equivalent = the same EXPRESSION. (Repair: equivalent = the same TOTAL with different expressions.)
Subtraction can't make positive numbers. (Children miss 75-25 = 50. Repair: explicit subtraction examples.)
Only 2-term expressions count. (Repair: 3-term expressions like 25+15+10 = 50 also work.)
recovery_moves: Always say 'find a DIFFERENT way' aloud. The word 'different' targets variety.
Use a chart with explicit slots for addend pairs. Visible structure prevents repetition.
Show subtraction examples. Variety is bigger when both operations are options.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of C2.3 (equivalent expressions for whole numbers to 100).

parts_outline.task: Make 50: list 8 different expressions that equal 50. Mix addition and subtraction.
Make 100: list 6 different expressions that equal 100.
Pick Your Target: pick a target number between 60 and 100. List 5 different expressions for it.
